records.title: AI capability is not the same as worker control
records.observation: The existing synthesis separates access to AI capability from control over tasks, worker welfare, and successful remedy.
records.mechanism: A tool can increase capability while leaving decision rights, measurement, and correction with an employer or platform.
limits: This is a synthesis boundary, not a pooled causal estimate.

records.title: AI access can reduce some work without changing all output
records.observation: The recorded evidence describes a field experiment across 66 firms and 7,137 knowledge workers in which AI access reduced email time and some work outside regular hours, without changing task quantity or composition.
records.mechanism: AI may remove one visible task while leaving the wider allocation of work and control unchanged.
limits: The record does not establish a universal productivity effect.
It does not by itself establish durable worker welfare or bargaining effects.

records.title: Company AI claims require separate outcome evidence
records.observation: The Atlas board separates company AI claims from independent outcome evidence and records open proof requirements rather than treating deployment language as realized benefit.
records.mechanism: Company adoption language can describe an input or intention without proving a customer, worker, or public outcome.
limits: The board is a research surface; it is not itself independent outcome evidence.

records.title: Capability can arrive with dependence
records.observation: The reader layer frames AI infrastructure as potentially building useful capability and dependence together, while keeping portability, exit, and state-control effects open.
records.mechanism: A service can make work possible while increasing reliance on a provider or system that the user cannot easily replace.
limits: The page preserves open questions about application migration, outcomes, portability, and exit.

records.title: Can workers and customers correct or leave AI-mediated systems?
records.observation: The first vertical slice still needs compatible evidence on correction, appeal, switching, and exit after an AI-mediated decision or workflow change.
records.mechanism: Control is incomplete if a person cannot understand, correct, or leave the system without losing ordinary access.
limits: This is a research request, not a finding.

insights.title: AI can return time without returning control
insights.plainLanguageSummary: The current evidence supports a narrower reading than 'AI makes work more productive': AI can remove visible tasks while decisions, measurement, correction, and dependence remain controlled by the employer or platform.
insights.strongestAlternative: The apparent control gap may be temporary because early deployments have not yet matured into stable workflow changes.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A compatible longitudinal study shows durable control, pay, and remedy improvements for affected workers.
Company and independent records show that workers can understand, correct, and leave AI-mediated decisions without material penalty.
insights.nextTest: Track one named AI-mediated workflow from company deployment through worker/customer use, correction, appeal, and exit evidence.
